claims.text: Sequential recommendation systems enable users to discover relevant items based on their past interactions.
Directly extracting representations from an LLM based on textual features does not guarantee semantic information preservation when fed into a sequential model.
Concatenating textual descriptions of item sequences into a long text for LLM recommendation results in lengthy token sequences.
Feeding long item sequence text representations into an LLM diminishes practical efficiency.

evidence.description: Sequential recommendation systems (SRS) are crucial in various applications as they enable users to discover relevant items based on their past interactions.

Specifically, directly extracting representations from an LLM based on items' textual features and feeding them into a sequential model hold no guarantee that the semantic information of texts could be preserved in these representations.
Additionally, concatenating textual descriptions of all items in an item sequence into a long text and feeding it into an LLM for recommendation results in lengthy token sequences...

limitations.text: Directly extracting representations from an LLM based on items' textual features and feeding them into a sequential model holds no guarantee that the semantic information of texts is preserved.
Concatenating textual descriptions of all items in an item sequence into a long text for LLM recommendation yields lengthy token sequences that diminish practical efficiency.
